'''Keith Gull''' (born 29 May 1948)<ref name=whoswho/> is a British microbiologist who is a [[Wellcome Trust Principal Research Fellow]] and Professor of [[Molecular microbiology]] at the [[Sir William Dunn School of Pathology]], [[University of Oxford]].  He was the principal of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]]<ref>http://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/index.php?section=47 The Principal, St. Edmund Hall, Oxford</ref> from 1 October 2009 to 30 September 2018, succeeding [[Michael Mingos]].<ref>[http://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/index.php?action=view&id=95&module=newsmodule&src=%40random41940a897e943 "The Hall elects its next Principal"], St Edmund Hall</ref><ref>[http://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/index.php?section=47 "SEH academic staff"], St Edmund Hall</ref>

== Education ==
Gull was educated at [[Gillbrook Academy|Eston Grammar School]] and [[King's College London]] where he was awarded a first class [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1969 followed by a [[PhD]] in 1973 supervised by [[Tony Trinci]].<ref name="phd">{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|first=Keith|last=Gull|publisher=London, Queen Elizabeth College|title=Studies on the effect of griseofulvin on fungal growth and cytology|year=1973|url=https://discover.libraryhub.jisc.ac.uk/search?q=Studies%20on%20the%20effect%20of%20griseofulvin%20on%20fungal%20growth%20and%20cytology&rn=1|oclc=681147643}}</ref><ref name=obit>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2020/nov/10/tony-trinci-obituary|first=Keith|last=Gull|year=2020|publisher=[[The Guardian]]|website=theguardian.com|title=Tony Trinci obituary}}</ref>

==Career and research==
On completion of his PhD, he moved to a lectureship at the [[University of Kent]]. He held a personal chair at Kent when he moved to the [[Victoria University of Manchester|University of Manchester]] where he spent the 1990s involved with the development of the School of Biological Sciences as Head of Biochemistry and Research Dean. He moved to Oxford in 2002. He was Chairman of the [[Biochemical Society]] (1999–2002), and is a trustee of [[Cancer Research UK]]. After nine years as Principal Professor of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]], Gull retired at the end of the 2017-18 academic year, and was succeeded by [[Kathy Willis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/events/celebration-keith-gull|title=A Celebration of Keith Gull|website=St Edmund Hall|language=en|access-date=2018-05-09|archive-date=15 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180415025110/https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/events/celebration-keith-gull|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="New principal 2018">{{cite web|url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2018-05-09-st-edmund-hall-elects-new-principal|title=St Edmund Hall elects new principal|date=9 May 2018 |publisher=ox.ac.uk|access-date=2 November 2018}}</ref>

===Controversy===
During his tenure as Principal of St Edmund Hall, he was alleged to have exploited college finances by claiming £500 in "Christmas presents" and "gifts" between November and December 2015, and £185 on a desk lamp in November 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cherwell.org/2018/05/18/old-boys-clubs-and-toilet-brushes-how-college-bosses-spend-your-money|title=Old boys' clubs and toilet brushes: how college bosses spend your money|website=Cherwell|date=18 May 2018|language=en|access-date=2018-06-10}}</ref> Gull defended his Christmas expenses claims, but not the desk lamp claim.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cherwell.org/2018/05/27/exposed-expenses-hide-a-darker-truth/|title=Exposed expenses hide a darker truth|website=Cherwell|date=27 May 2018|language=en|access-date=2018-05-27}}</ref>

In 2010, Gull attracted criticism by his students and the national press for the decision to spend £15,000 on a college snowdrop garden amid budget cuts. He defended the decision, claiming the snowdrops will be "fantastic", but apologised for the way in which it was made.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oxfordstudent.com/2010/05/14/fury-sprouts-over-snowdrop-garden/|title=Fury sprouts over snowdrop garden|website=Cherwell|date=14 May 2010|language=en|access-date=2010-05-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/educationnews/7704039/Oxford-college-in-row-over-15000-field-of-snowdrops.html|title=Oxford college in row over £15,000 field of snowdrops|website=The Telegraph|date=10 May 2010 |language=en|access-date=2010-05-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/education/education-news/oxford-students-hit-out-at-16315000-snowdrop-field-1970007.html|title=Oxford students hit out at £15,000 snowdrop field|website=The Telegraph|date=9 May 2010 |language=en|access-date=2010-05-10}}</ref>

In 2015, Gull declined requests to clarify the status of claims made by [[Bongbong Marcos]], son of Filipino dictator [[Ferdinand Marcos]], about whether he finished his degree at [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/investigative/84397-bongbong-marcos-degrees-oxford-wharton/|title=EXCLUSIVE: Did Bongbong Marcos lie about Oxford, Wharton?|website=Rappler|date=24 February 2015 |language=en|access-date=2015-02-25}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Among numerous prizes, fellowships, and other awards, Keith Gull was awarded the [[Marjory Stephenson Prize]] from the [[Society for General Microbiology]] (1996), was elected Fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]] (1999), elected [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2003|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2003]],<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150916140708/https://royalsociety.org/people/keith-gull-11555|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/keith-gull-11555/|archive-date=2015-09-16|title=Professor Keith Gull CBE FMedSci FRS|publisher=Royal Society}}</ref> and was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in the 2004 [[New Year Honours]] list for services to microbiology.<ref>http://www.london-gazette.co.uk/issues/57155/supplements/8 "New Year Honours List 2004"</ref> He holds an honorary [[Doctor of Science]] from the [[University of Kent]]. His certificate of election to the [[Royal Society]] reads: {{centred pull quote|Distinguished for his contributions to our understanding of the cell and molecular biology of eukaryotic microbes, especially fungi, [[slime mould]]s and [[trypanosomes]]. His work has provided important insights into how cells construct their [[cytoskeleton]]s by modulating [[tubulin]] [[gene expression]] and protein modification. His novel approaches have led to discovery of unusual mechanisms of [[microtubule]] initiation and the partitioning of genomes in [[African trypanosomiasis|sleeping sickness]] trypanosomes, also of the relationship of division to differentiation in these parasites. His discovery of the mode of action of the antifungal agent [[griseofulvin]] has been followed by explanations of the selective toxicity and resistance mechanisms of [[fungicide]]s and [[anthelminthic]]s.<ref name=royal>{{cite web |url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC/2003/18%27) |title=Certificate of Election EC/2003/18: Keith Gull |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=18 September 2015 |archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/6be2ZgRWJ?url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%3D%27EC%2F2003%2F18%27%29 |location=London |url-status=dead |access-date=15 February 2020 }}</ref>}}

Gull was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) in 2010.<ref name=embo/>
